People presenting with type 2 diabetes who have lower initial fasting plasma glucose (FPG) levels may experience fewer adverse clinical outcomes despite similar glycemic progression. Since most individuals with type 2 diabetes are asymptomatic at diagnosis, active case detection programs would be required to identify those early in the course of their disease.

This association suggests that detecting and managing even impaired fasting blood glucose levels preoperatively could lead to improved patient outcomes after certain medical procedures, such as coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery.
